newsitem.title: UK: Wessex wants windfall tax to favour strong.
newsitem.headline: Wessex wants windfall tax to favour strong.

text.p: British water utility Wessex Water Plc wants a one-off tax proposed by the new Labour government to favour companies which have performed well, chairman Nicholas Hood told Reuters in a telephone interview.

"Those companies which have performed very well by not having any exceptional provisions for instance for non-core activities, by not having restructuring provisions...should not be penalised, they should be favoured," he said.

The government, which has a huge majority, has vowed to impose a one-off tax on the "excess profits" of privatised utilities with details of its size and scope expected to be announced in a first budget on July 2.
He said those companies which had had "substantial losses or substantial provisions for losses, should not be favoured."
As a result, Wessex felt the tax should be based on an earlier valuation, "closer to privatisation than maybe current valuations."
He said the company's current share price, "relatively high" compared with the rest of the sector, reflected its good performance.
Wessex shares were trading up 4.5 pence at 391 pence by 0754 GMT.
"If you're just going to take current valuation (as a base for the tax) it would be unfair on our shareholders and on our staff and customers too," he said.
"Most of all...it should be fair," he added.
